claims_in_article.decontextualised_claim_text: Venezuela faces profound political and economic uncertainty in the wake of the US military intervention that captured Nicolás Maduro on 3 January.
Output held just under 3 million barrels per day through much of the 2000s, before sliding under Maduro —a decline that accelerated sharply after US unilateral sanctions targeting the oil sector.
Mulino took a more cautious approach, drawing a direct parallel to Panama's 1989 invasion to capture Manuel Noriega.
